items.native_evidence_gate: .github/workflows/browse-daemon-native.yml: all six declared runners must execute nonzero daemon tests, lifecycle, 50x50 competing starts and supplemental real Go/Rust requests; retain raw logs and hashed process receipts. Historical 652453d oracle is unchanged; dcddcef0 adds process observations only. The same six jobs also run all workspace tests through source-verified, newly Go-generated historical-input MCP fixtures and a production Rust daemon; thirteen actual CLI outputs and three actual failure controls must pass. Registry/autostart additionally require daemon_registry.py Go API, 108 CLI observations (including 48 invalid-session CLI failures) and 20 raw frames per binary, eight actual concurrent clients, retained Go migration-file bytes and six rejecting controls on all six native runners. State-key successor additionally requires daemon_state_key.py 31 Linux/Windows or38 Darwin startup pairs, all six persisted historical files unchanged during inspection, destructive authenticated cleanup/stop-order proofs, real Store warning observations, three rejecting executable controls, and owned security-exit44 absence fixtures for every Darwin process/workspace test.
items.remaining_scope: Issue #772 remains open/in_progress: this candidate connects existing Core providers once before IPC and shares a keyed Store between browser and metadata handlers. Independent full review and six fresh native OS/architecture receipts are pending. Runtime/default-release cutover remains gated; registry/Core historical parity alone does not close this issue. Fresh snapshot same-name encrypted overwrite retains observed Go behavior with warning; a future explicit fail-closed overwrite contract requires separate evidence and decision, never an undocumented E012 exception. The confirmed4cd startup provider orphan is corrected only through explicit CLI startup lifetime ownership; private provider process groups/Windows jobs and actual descendant/sibling controls remain subject to independent/native approval. The separately reproduced inherited root-prefix --session spelling gap already exists in b363 and remains open for its own compatibility correction. Local macOS arm64 receipt (2026-11-08, base ba4c45d62): cargo test -p symbrowse-daemon --locked, port/harness/run.py --suite daemon and --suite daemon-races --repeat 50 pass; workspace clippy and tests pass. Unix-socket tests need a short TMPDIR (macOS sun_path limit); launchers with a long TMPDIR fail them for environmental reasons only. daemon_state_key.py needs the removed pinned Go oracle and cannot run; per the 2026-11-09 maintainer decision it is replaced by port/harness/daemon_state_key_replay.py, which replays the sealed Linux Go recording (migration/evidence/browse-state-key-772/candidate-4cd, sealed by its pinned retention.json) against the Rust daemon without Go. Local macOS arm64 replay (2026-11-09): 31/31 startup cases match, 3/3 executable controls rejected, store probe matches; the browse-daemon-native workflow runs the replay on Linux amd64/arm64 and macOS. Linux CI receipts for the replay and independent review remain pending, so the item stays in_progress.

items.title: Static DOM, rendering, relevance, cache and recovery
items.stop_rule: Do not select a renderer until the complete corpus passes; unexplained byte differences are not normalizable.
acceptance: 2026-11-13 macOS arm64 (base de2989174): python3 port/harness/run.py --suite fetch-render --comparison bytes passes (render_corpus 1/1 over 28 vectors, static_controls 5/5, pipeline_controls 8/8); cargo nextest run -p symbrowse-fetch --locked = 91/91 passed. No byte difference exists: no Rust renderer change was needed.

Corpus provenance re-proven 2026-11-13: the pre-removal Go generator scripts/rust-port/fetch_fixture_gen.go and internal/fetch tree from dde8cced1^ were rebuilt (go 1.27.4) and re-run; the regenerated static.json has identical oracle_commit, source_digest 4924c029...50ac1, vector_count 28 and value-identical JSON for every field of all 28 vectors. Raw bytes differ only in how Go spells U+FFFD in JSON strings (the committed file mixes escaped and literal forms); the Rust test compares parsed values, so no normalization of rendered output is involved.

items.title: Safari attach and BiDi adapters
items.stop_rule: Keep Safari cfg-gated; stop if the port adds a privilege or installation contract.
items.remaining_scope: 2026-11-08 macOS arm64: Safari attach/BiDi and Firefox unit and contract tests pass. Safari needs Remote Automation on the user's real Safari, which an agent must not drive (maintainer gate). 2026-11-09 Firefox native gate (no geckodriver; the adapter launches Firefox with BiDi directly): the adapter now owns a fresh browsingContext.create tab because Firefox 159 rejects evaluation in the first context of a new profile ("System access is required"); the symbrowse-firefox-spike gate passes on macOS arm64 against Firefox 159.0.1 for a fresh blank tab and a loopback http navigation. .github/workflows/browse-firefox-native.yml runs the same gate on Linux amd64 and macOS; its receipt is pending. Firefox native gate receipt: browse-firefox-native.yml green on linux-amd64 and darwin-arm64; local re-run 2026-11-10 on macOS arm64 against Firefox 159.0.1 passes (unit tests 2/2, blank-tab and loopback-navigation spike, production-daemon firefox_native test 1/1). Firefox BiDi is therefore advertised on macOS and Linux only (symbrowse-core advertise module: --engine validation, daemon capabilities handshake; typed engine_not_advertised elsewhere). Safari is NOT advertised and stays cfg-gated: its native gate needs Remote Automation on the user's real Safari, a maintainer step. Item stays in_progress until that Safari gate passes.
